Title: HTTP/3 Flood Detection Bypass and Unbounded Processing
Analysis:
A vulnerability exists in the HTTP/3 protocol handler where the total_bytes and payload_bytes session state counters can grow excessively or cause incorrect flow/flood control calculations if a client sends a large volume of empty headers or constructs frames that trigger asymmetric tracking. Specifically, in `ngx_http_v3_request.c`, `h3c->payload_bytes` is incremented by the length of the parsed field:
`h3c->payload_bytes += ngx_http_v3_encode_field_l(NULL, &st->field_rep.field.name, &st->field_rep.field.value);`
whereas `h3c->total_bytes` tracks the raw buffer consumption:
`h3c->total_bytes += b->pos - p;`
An attacker can exploit this discrepancy by feeding HTTP/3 headers or control frames designed to bypass flood checks (`total_bytes / 8 > payload_bytes + 1048576`) or trigger CPU spikes/denial of service, as the ratio of total bytes to payload bytes is used for detecting HTTP/3 floods in `ngx_http_v3_check_flood()`. In some conditions, it might be possible to manipulate the ratio by packing massive QPACK field instructions that do not map to equivalent payload increases, or by supplying large names/values that are decompressed/looked up and bloat the session or header limits.
